Repository: /luxon (the Luxon date/time library, JavaScript, tested with Jest).

BUG REPORT: There is a bug in `src/interval.js` in the static method `Interval.fromISO(text, opts)`. When `Settings.throwOnInvalid` is true, `Interval.fromISO` should still be able to parse inputs like `<start>/<duration>` or `<duration>/<end>` (e.g. "2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/P1Y2M10DT2H30M") and inputs that are entirely unparsable should throw an `InvalidIntervalError`. Currently, with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true`, the calls to `DateTime.fromISO(s, opts)` / `DateTime.fromISO(e, opts)` throw `InvalidDateTimeError` before the code can fall back to interpreting the other half as a `Duration`, so valid duration-based ISO intervals fail, and the thrown error type is wrong.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR: the test `Interval.fromISO works with Settings.throwOnInvalid` should pass. It is not present in the repository; its name describes the expected behaviour. Reasonable expected behaviour: with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true`, `Interval.fromISO("2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/P1Y2M10DT2H30M")` returns a valid Interval, and `Interval.fromISO("bad")` throws `InvalidIntervalError` (from src/errors.js).

TASK:
1. Read /luxon/src/interval.js (the `fromISO` method, around lines 134-157), /luxon/src/datetime.js (`DateTime.fromISO`, `DateTime.invalid`), /luxon/src/duration.js (`Duration.fromISO`), /luxon/src/settings.js, /luxon/src/errors.js, and /luxon/test/interval/*.js.
2. Fix the bug in `src/interval.js` ONLY. The minimal, correct fix is to guard the `DateTime.fromISO` calls with try/catch so that a thrown InvalidDateTimeError is treated as "not valid", letting the code fall through to the Duration interpretation, and finally to `Interval.invalid(...)` which throws `InvalidIntervalError` when `Settings.throwOnInvalid` is true. Do not change any other file. Do not edit or delete any existing test.
3. Run the test suite to verify: `cd /luxon && npx jest test/interval` and also the full suite `cd /luxon && npx jest` (or `npm test`). Record which tests fail BEFORE and AFTER your change.
4. Write a small ad-hoc check (e.g. a temp file run with jest or node, delete it afterwards) proving that with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true`, `Interval.fromISO("2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/P1Y2M10DT2H30M")` works and `Interval.fromISO("bad")` throws InvalidIntervalError.

CONSTRAINTS: Make no other changes anywhere in the repo. Do not modify existing tests. No new features.

REPORT BACK: the exact diff you applied, the before/after test results (list of failing test names), and the output of your ad-hoc verification.

Verification task in the repository /luxon (Luxon date/time library, Jest tests). Do NOT change any source file unless you find a real problem; your job is to verify, not to redesign.

Context: `src/interval.js` was just modified so that `Interval.fromISO` catches errors from `DateTime.fromISO` (which throws when `Settings.throwOnInvalid` is true) and treats that half as invalid, falling through to the Duration interpretation and finally to `Interval.invalid(...)`.

Do the following and report raw command output:
1. `cd /luxon && git status --porcelain && git diff` — report the exact diff (only src/interval.js should be modified; no test files touched, no leftover temp files).
2. `cd /luxon && npx jest test/interval 2>&1 | tail -30` — report the summary.
3. `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40` — report the summary and the names of any failing tests.
4. Independently write a THROWAWAY jest test file at /luxon/test/interval/verify.tmp.test.js that checks, with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` (restore in `finally`): (a) `Interval.fromISO("2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/P1Y2M10DT2H30M").isValid === true`, (b) `Interval.fromISO("P1Y2M10DT2H30M/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z").isValid === true`, (c) `Interval.fromISO("2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z").isValid === true`, (d) `expect(() => Interval.fromISO("bad")).toThrow(InvalidIntervalError)` importing InvalidIntervalError from "../../src/errors.js", (e) `expect(() => Interval.fromISO("foo/bar")).toThrow(InvalidIntervalError)`. Run it with `npx jest test/interval/verify.tmp.test.js`, report output, then DELETE the temp file and confirm `git status --porcelain` shows only ` M src/interval.js`.
5. Also report whether `Interval.fromISO("2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/bad")` with throwOnInvalid=true throws, and what error class it throws (just informational).

REPORT BACK: raw outputs for steps 1-5 and a clear verdict on whether the fix works and whether any pre-existing test regressed.

DIAGNOSTIC TASK ONLY — DO NOT EDIT ANY FILE. Repository: /luxon (Luxon date/time library). Another agent is concurrently editing /luxon/src/impl/util.js, so you must NOT modify anything; only read and run commands.

GOAL: Find the exact input for which `DateTime#plus` (and/or `#minus`) produces a wrong result around the year-100 barrier when the span passes through February, and identify which function in `src/impl/util.js` is responsible.

BACKGROUND: A hidden test named `DateTime#plus works across the 100 barrier when passing through February` is expected to pass after a bug in `src/impl/util.js` is fixed. The existing visible tests are `DateTime#plus works across the 100 barrier` (test/datetime/math.test.js:92, `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 2 })` → 0100-01-02) and the matching `#minus` test at line 169.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Read /luxon/src/impl/util.js (especially `isLeapYear`, `daysInYear`, `daysInMonth`, `objToLocalTS`, `floorMod`), /luxon/src/datetime.js (`adjustTime` around line 124, `objToTS`, `fixOffset`, `plus`, `minus`), and /luxon/src/impl/conversions.js.
2. Write a THROWAWAY node/jest script (e.g. /tmp/diag.test.js run via `cd /luxon && npx jest /tmp/diag.test.js` — if jest refuses files outside the root, put it at /luxon/test/diag.tmp.test.js and DELETE it when done) that:
   a. For years y in 90..110 and for every month/day, computes `DateTime.fromISO(iso).plus({days:1})`, `.plus({months:1})`, `.plus({years:1})`, `.plus({days:60})`, `.minus({days:1})`, `.minus({months:1})` and compares the resulting y/m/d against an independent reference computed with plain JS `Date` in UTC using explicit `setUTCFullYear` (build the reference by constructing `new Date(Date.UTC(y, m-1, d))`, then `setUTCFullYear(y)` to avoid the 19xx remapping, then add/subtract with setUTCDate/setUTCMonth/setUTCFullYear) — report every mismatch with the exact input string, the operation, the actual result and the expected result.
   b. Also directly evaluate `isLeapYear` semantics: for y in 90..110 print `DateTime.utc(y, 2, 28).daysInMonth` and `DateTime.utc(y,2,28).isInLeapYear` and compare with the proleptic Gregorian rule (divisible by 4 and not by 100, unless by 400).
   c. Also print the results of these specific calls: `DateTime.fromISO("0100-01-31").plus({months:1})`, `DateTime.fromISO("0100-02-28").plus({days:1})`, `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({days:59})`, `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({days:60})`, `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({days:61})`, `DateTime.fromISO("0099-11-30").plus({months:3})`, `DateTime.fromISO("0100-03-01").minus({days:1})`, `DateTime.fromISO("0100-01-01").minus({days:1})` — each as `.toISODate()`.
3. Delete any temp file you created and confirm `git status --porcelain` shows only ` M src/interval.js` (plus possibly ` M src/impl/util.js` from the other agent) — never leave temp files.

REPORT BACK: the exact list of mismatching inputs (input, operation, actual, expected), your conclusion about which util.js function is buggy and what the correct code should be, and the raw output of the specific calls in 2c. Do not edit any file.

Repository: /luxon (the Luxon date/time library, JavaScript, tested with Jest).

BUG REPORT: There is a bug in `src/impl/util.js`. Once it is fixed, the test `DateTime#plus works across the 100 barrier when passing through February` should pass. That test is NOT present in the repository; its name describes the expected behaviour. Expected behaviour: adding a duration (e.g. months/years) to a DateTime in a low year (around year 100) that passes through February must produce the correct date — the leap-year rule for the Julian/Gregorian boundary and the 4/100/400 leap rules must be handled correctly by whatever helper in `src/impl/util.js` decides whether a year is a leap year (look for something like `isLeapYear`). Note: the real-world expectation is the proleptic Gregorian rule: a year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, unless divisible by 100, unless also divisible by 400. The likely bug is that the year-100 special case is handled backwards or that the code special-cases years < 100 incorrectly.

TASK:
1. Read /luxon/src/impl/util.js in full, plus /luxon/src/impl/conversions.js (which uses the leap-year helper), /luxon/src/datetime.js (`plus`, `daysInMonth`, `isInLeapYear`), and the existing tests in /luxon/test/datetime/*.js that mention leap years or the year 100 (grep for `isLeapYear`, `leap`, `100`).
2. Work out the exact intended semantics from in-repo evidence: docstrings, existing tests, and the mathematical definition of a leap year. Then fix the bug in `src/impl/util.js` ONLY (minimal change). Do not modify any other source file and do NOT edit, delete or add tests permanently.
3. Verify: `cd /luxon && npx jest test/datetime 2>&1 | tail -40` and the full suite `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40`. Record failing test names BEFORE (use `git stash` to compare if useful, then restore) and AFTER your change. IMPORTANT: two tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js ('DateTime#toFormat(\'FFF\') returns a medium date/time representation without seconds' and the 'FFFF' one) are known pre-existing failures caused by the container's ICU version — they must remain the only failures.
4. Write a THROWAWAY jest test at /luxon/test/datetime/tmpverify.test.js named exactly "DateTime#plus works across the 100 barrier when passing through February" that checks the expected behaviour, e.g. that `DateTime.local(100, 1, 31).plus({ months: 1 })` gives February 28 (100 is not a leap year under the proleptic Gregorian rule) and that `DateTime.local(100, 2, 28).plus({ days: 1 })` gives March 1, and that `DateTime.local(104, 2, 28).plus({ days: 1 })` gives February 29 (104 IS a leap year). Also check `DateTime.local(100, 2, 28).isInLeapYear === false` and `DateTime.local(104, 2, 28).isInLeapYear === true`. Run it with `npx jest test/datetime/tmpverify.test.js`, report the output, then DELETE the temp file and confirm `git status --porcelain` shows only ` M src/impl/util.js`.

REPORT BACK: the exact diff, before/after test results (names of failing tests), the temp test output, and confirmation that no pre-existing test regressed.

BUG REPORT: There is a bug in `src/duration.js`. Once it is fixed, the test `Duration#normalize can convert all unit pairs` should pass. That test is NOT present in the repository; its name describes the expected behaviour. Expected behaviour: `Duration.fromObject({ [from]: 1 }).normalize().toObject()` (or `.as(to)` / `.shiftTo(to)`) must correctly convert between EVERY pair of duration units — years, quarters, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds — in both directions, using the library's documented conversion matrices (see the `casualMatrix` / `accurateMatrix` in src/duration.js and docs/math.md). A likely bug: one entry in one of the conversion matrices is wrong or missing (e.g. a wrong number of milliseconds for a unit, or a missing `quarters` entry), so some unit pair converts incorrectly.

TASK:
1. Read /luxon/src/duration.js in full (especially the `casualMatrix`, `accurateMatrix`, `normalizeUnit`, `normalize`, `as`, `shiftTo`, `toObject` methods), /luxon/src/impl/conversions.js, docs/math.md (the conversion tables) and the existing tests in /luxon/test/duration/*.js (grep for `normalize`, `shiftTo`, `as(`).
2. Empirically find the wrong conversion: write a THROWAWAY jest test at /luxon/test/duration/diag.tmp.test.js that, for every ordered pair (from, to) of the 9 units, computes `Duration.fromObject({ [from]: 1 }).as(to)` and `Duration.fromObject({ [from]: 1 }).normalize().toObject()`, and compares against the value implied by the documented conversion table in docs/math.md and the matrix in src/duration.js. Report every inconsistency you find. Note: `normalize()` only rolls up units that are present, so to test all pairs you may need `Duration.fromObject({ [from]: 1 }).shiftTo(to)` or `.as(to)`.
3. Fix the bug with a MINIMAL change to `src/duration.js` ONLY. Do not modify any test file, do not add features. Another agent may be concurrently editing src/datetime.js and src/impl/util.js — do NOT touch those files.
4. Verify: `cd /luxon && npx jest test/duration 2>&1 | tail -30` and the full suite `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40`. IMPORTANT: two tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js ('DateTime#toFormat(\'FFF\') returns a medium date/time representation without seconds' and the 'FFFF' one) are known PRE-EXISTING failures caused by the container's ICU version — they must remain the only failures.
5. Write a THROWAWAY jest test at /luxon/test/duration/norm.tmp.test.js named exactly "Duration#normalize can convert all unit pairs" that loops over all ordered pairs of units and asserts the conversions are consistent with the documented table; run it, report the output, then DELETE both temp files and confirm `git status --porcelain` shows only the expected modified source files.

REPORT BACK: the exact diff, which unit pair was wrong and what the correct value is, before/after test results (names of failing tests), the temp test output, and confirmation that no pre-existing test regressed.

BUG REPORT: There is a bug in `src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js`. Once it is fixed, these two tests should pass: `A DateTime in an invalid FixedOffsetZone is itself invalid` and `FixedOffsetZone is invalid when constructed with a non-numeric offset`. Those tests are NOT present in the repository; their names describe the expected behaviour.

Expected behaviour: `FixedOffsetZone.instance("bogus")` (i.e. constructing a FixedOffsetZone with a non-numeric offset such as a string that is not a number) must produce an INVALID zone — `zone.isValid === false` — and a DateTime created in that zone must itself be invalid. The likely bug: the `isValid` getter (or the constructor / `instance` static / `offset` handling) does not detect a non-numeric offset, e.g. `isValid` returns `true` unconditionally, or the offset is not validated with `isNumber`.

TASK:
1. Read /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js in full, plus /luxon/src/zones/invalidZone.js, /luxon/src/zones/IANAZone.js (for how it implements `isValid`), /luxon/src/impl/zoneUtil.js, /luxon/src/datetime.js (how a zone's `isValid` makes a DateTime invalid — search for `unsupported zone` / `zone.isValid`), /luxon/src/impl/util.js (`isNumber`), and the existing tests: /luxon/test/zones/fixedOffsetZone.test.js and /luxon/test/datetime/zone.test.js (grep for `FixedOffsetZone`, `isValid`, `unsupported zone`).
2. Determine the correct behaviour from in-repo evidence (docstrings, the parallel IANAZone/InvalidZone implementations, existing tests). Then fix the bug with a MINIMAL change to `src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js` ONLY. Do not modify any test file, do not add features. Other agents are concurrently editing src/datetime.js, src/duration.js and src/impl/util.js — do NOT touch those files.
3. Verify: `cd /luxon && npx jest test/zones test/datetime 2>&1 | tail -40` and the full suite `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40`. IMPORTANT: two tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js ('DateTime#toFormat(\'FFF\') returns a medium date/time representation without seconds' and the 'FFFF' one) are known PRE-EXISTING failures caused by the container's ICU version — they must remain the only failures.
4. Write a THROWAWAY jest test at /luxon/test/zones/fixed.tmp.test.js with the two test names exactly `A DateTime in an invalid FixedOffsetZone is itself invalid` and `FixedOffsetZone is invalid when constructed with a non-numeric offset`, asserting `FixedOffsetZone.instance("bogus").isValid === false` and that a DateTime built in that zone is invalid. Run it, report the output, then DELETE the temp file and confirm `git status --porcelain` shows only the expected modified source files.

REPORT BACK: the exact diff, before/after test results (names of failing tests), the temp test output, and confirmation that no pre-existing test regressed.

Repository: /luxon (the Luxon date/time library, JavaScript, tested with Jest).

BUG REPORT: There is a bug in `src/datetime.js`. Once it is fixed, the test `DateTime#isInDST() returns true for 1974 whole year in USA- from January 6th to October 27th` should pass. That test is NOT present in the repository; its name describes the expected behaviour.

Expected behaviour: in the USA, 1974 had year-round daylight saving time (the US Emergency Daylight Saving Time Energy Conservation Act): DST began on 1974-01-06 and effectively ran through 1974-10-27 (when standard time resumed). So for the IANA zone `America/New_York`, `DateTime.fromISO("1974-01-06T00:00", { zone: "America/New_York" }).isInDST()` should be true, and so should every instant from 1974-01-06 up to (but not including) 1974-10-27, e.g. `DateTime.fromISO("1974-06-01T12:00", { zone: "America/New_York" }).isInDST()` should be true. Presumably the current code computes DST-ness by comparing the offset against the offset of the same date in January and July (`getters.js`/`datetime.js` `isInDST`), which fails when both January and July are in DST.

TASK:
1. Read /luxon/src/datetime.js (search for `isInDST`), /luxon/src/zones/IANAZone.js, /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js, /luxon/src/zone.js, /luxon/src/impl/zoneUtil.js, and the existing tests in /luxon/test/datetime/ (grep for `isInDST`) and /luxon/test/zones/.
2. Determine the correct implementation of `isInDST()` from in-repo evidence (docstrings, existing tests, the semantics of DST). Note: `DateTime#isInDST()` is documented as 'Returns whether the DateTime is in daylight saving time'. A robust implementation compares the zone's offset at this instant with the zone's offset at the same instant minus the DST adjustment, or compares with the offset in January/July but handles the case where the offset is the same in both (i.e. the zone is in DST for the whole year or has no DST).
3. Fix the bug with a MINIMAL change. Only touch `src/datetime.js` (and, if strictly necessary, the zone files) — do not modify any test file, do not add features, do not reformat unrelated code.
4. Verify: `cd /luxon && npx jest test/datetime test/zones 2>&1 | tail -40` and the full suite `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -40`. IMPORTANT: two tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js ('DateTime#toFormat(\'FFF\') returns a medium date/time representation without seconds' and the 'FFFF' one) are known PRE-EXISTING failures caused by the container's ICU version — they must remain the only failures. Also note another agent may be concurrently editing src/impl/util.js; do not touch that file.
5. Write a THROWAWAY jest test at /luxon/test/datetime/dst.tmp.test.js named exactly "DateTime#isInDST() returns true for 1974 whole year in USA- from January 6th to October 27th" that asserts: for America/New_York, `DateTime.fromISO("1974-01-06T00:00").isInDST()` is true, `DateTime.fromISO("1974-06-01T12:00").isInDST()` is true, `DateTime.fromISO("1974-10-27T01:00").isInDST()` is true, and `DateTime.fromISO("1974-11-01T12:00").isInDST()` is false, and `DateTime.fromISO("1974-01-05T12:00").isInDST()` is false. (Use `{ zone: "America/New_York" }`.) Run it, report the output, then DELETE the temp file and confirm `git status --porcelain` shows only the expected modified source files.

REPORT BACK: the exact diff, before/after test results (names of any failing tests), the temp test output, and confirmation that no pre-existing test regressed.
